Subject: Temporary retention hold request & backup purge timing

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — appreciated. Our compliance team ran into an audit workflow with a large enterprise customer that requires an extended log and snapshot window for a scoped set of workloads for the month of September.

Can Redwood do a temporary retention hold for the affected dataset (customer ID: ST-7782) that postpones the scheduled backup purge for up to 60 days beyond the current SLA? We need:
- An official timeline for the purge delay (start/end dates)
- The set of backup snapshots that will be preserved (IDs or time ranges is fine)
- Evidence that a subprocessor (HelixOps) will not delete artifacts during the hold

We are preparing an addendum to our DPA but need Redwood's operational commitment to avoid accidental purge during our audit window. Attach: compliance-checklist_v1.docx (requesting a checklist of the evidence you can share).

Can you confirm whether this needs a formal exec approval or if your standard GRC flow covers it?

Thanks,
Erin Matthews
Head of Compliance, Starlite Health
Attachments: compliance-checklist_v1.docx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention hold request & backup purge timing

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. I've looped in Legal (Kimberly), GRC (Neha), and Ops (Marcus) to scope the approval path.

High level options we can offer quickly:
1) Short exception (up to 30 days): operational approval from Ops + GRC signoff. No contract change required; we log the exception and lock the purge schedule for the listed snapshot IDs.
2) Extended exception (31–90 days): requires a DPA addendum / signature (covers liability & escrow terms) + Ops + Legal + GRC approvals. We recommend this route for anything >30 days.

For either option we will provide:
- A list of snapshot timestamps (we'll identify the affected snapshots once you confirm the exact resource IDs)
- An immutable short-term escrow snapshot (optional) for higher assurance (14-day immutable retention)
- An operational rollback plan if the audit finishes early

I've attached a draft purge timeline (proposed-purge-timeline-v1.pdf) with both options and the operational controls we'd apply. Please confirm which option Starlite prefers; if you choose extended, please send the signed addendum back when ready so Legal can fast-track.

Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the forward — my guidance below (inline):

> If Starlite picks option 1 (<=30 days): Ops + GRC can approve in day-of; Log exception record + temporary flag on the subprocessor parcel.
Fair — Ops/GRC can take this on. Make sure the exception record includes scope by resource ID and a scheduled review date.

> If Starlite picks option 2 (>30 days up to 90): we should require a DPA addendum + Legal sign-off. Also recommend creating an immutable escrow snapshot for the most sensitive IDs for 14 days to give their auditors an auditable image.
Agreed — for anything >30 days we need:
- Signed DPA addendum that references retention carveout + liability language
- Dataflow diagram showing HelixOps' role (subprocessor) and where snapshots are stored

Actionable items for Ops (Marcus):
- Prepare a labeled snapshot escrow process: create immutable snapshot (14 days) and a non-destructive lock on the original backups
- Provide list of exact artifacts we can share for evidence (audit logs, snapshot digests, lock events)

I think we can turn around option 1 immediately if Erin confirms. For option 2, Legal (me) will review the DPA addendum within 24h of receipt.

Team — quick ops plan and timing, based on both options:

Option 1 (<=30 days) — expedited path:
- Day 0 (on confirmation): Tag snapshots with retention-exception:ST-7782, disable scheduled purge job for those IDs.
- Day 0–30: Maintain audit log entries (actor, timestamp, original-purge-schedule).
- Day 31: If no extension requested, automatically enqueue purge with 72h notice to Starlite.

Option 2 (31–90 days) — contract path + escrow:
- On receipt of signed addendum: create an immutable escrow snapshot (retained for 14 days) plus retention-exception flag on originals.
- Maintain continuous audit trail; provide a daily digest to Starlite's compliance mailbox (starlite-compliance@starlitehealth.com) while exception is active.
- Rollback triggers: signed release from Starlite or expiration of exception window.

Required artifacts we'll provide (attachments / evidence):
- snapshot-manifest.csv (IDs + timestamps)
- lock-event-log.txt (actor/timestamp/reason)
- immutable-escrow-checksum.txt

I'll stand up the lock and daily digest once we receive the scoped IDs. ETA to have procedures & Ops-runbook: EOD tomorrow (2026-08-04).

-Marcus
